key_insight: crystALL generates diverse candidate crystal ensembles beyond the convex hull, prioritizing stable and metastable structures rather than ground-state stability alone.
engineering_relevance: Broader candidate ensembles can help engineers interpret experimental phases and investigate materials whose properties depend on metastable configurations.
method: Generate candidates through species substitutions, including searches across anonymized composition ranges.
Analyze candidates in ML feature space using pySIPFENN and cluster them to select representatives.
Use energy minimization or property matching to assemble ensembles for experimental or ab initio validation.
evidence_signal: The approach draws on 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD; the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy or runtime benchmarks.
watch_item: Candidate diversity does not establish thermodynamic populations or kinetic accessibility; downstream validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
